shapeRule._why: Spec 35 §3.1 names the threshold as the open gap this row exists to close.
shapeRule._corrected_2026_08_19_v1: The FIRST version of this rule (flat 'optionCount<=5 AND every label<=14 chars') was WRONG — caught live by Bean looking at a real 5-option ToggleGroupControl screenshot (sgs/icon-list Marker Type: Icon/Emoji/Bullet/Numbered/None) where 'Bullet', 'Numbered' and 'None' visibly ran together. Root cause confirmed via live DOM measurement: ToggleGroupControl divides its available width EQUALLY by option count (at 5 options, each segment is only 47px), so the same label length that fits comfortably at 2 options does not fit at 5.
shapeRule._corrected_2026_08_19_v2: The SECOND version (a strict px-per-character formula extrapolated from that ONE 'Numbered' data point — predicting only ~3-4 chars fit at 5 options) was ALSO too strict, per Bean's own live judgement after seeing it: 'I think 6 or 7 characters fits fine with 5 options.' A second real example confirmed this is the right read: sgs/container's 'Content band width' control (Normal/Wide/'Full (no cap)'/'Custom…', 4 options) shows 'Custom…' (7 chars, an intentionally-authored label with its ellipsis baked into the source text, not CSS truncation — confirmed by reading WidthPanel.js:29, NOT a bug) rendering CLEANLY with zero overflow, while 'Full (no cap)' (13 chars, two words) wraps to two lines. A single fixed px-per-character constant derived from one word ('Numbered') does not transfer cleanly to a different word ('Custom…') — real rendered text width varies per-character, not by a flat average. Rather than manufacture false precision from 2-3 data points, this row now states the rule as Bean calibrated it directly, with both confirming and refuting real examples as evidence.
shapeRule._corrected_2026_08_19_v3: The THIRD and current version adds the LINE-COUNT ceiling Bean identified after seeing the deployed control: 'if the text also goes to 3 lines in a single box it should switch to the dropdown version too. In the example it's touching the top and bottom borders of the box.' v2 described 'Full (no cap)' as wrapping to TWO lines — that was an eyeball estimate and it was WRONG. Measured live 2026-08-19 via Range.getClientRects() on the real deployed control (the only method that returns true rendered line boxes; element height does not, because the span stretches to fill its segment): it renders THREE lines. That is the difference between 'a bit tight' and 'physically cannot fit', and it makes the rule mechanically checkable instead of a judgement call.
shapeRule.rule: Segmented (ToggleGroupControl) requires ALL THREE: (a) at most 5 options; (b) NO label renders on 3+ lines inside its segment (vertical overflow); (c) NO label's rendered line is wider than its segment (horizontal overflow). Any single label failing (b) or (c) forces SelectControl (dropdown) for the WHOLE control. Both are measured on the rendered control, not predicted from character count — character count only hints at the risk, geometry decides it. As a rough authoring guide, a short single unbroken word of ~6-7 characters reliably fits (confirmed live: 'Bullet' 6 chars at n=5; 'Custom…' 7 chars at n=4 with only 4px horizontal spare, so treat 7 as the practical ceiling).

twoDistinctFailureModes._why: ⛔ These are NOT the same defect and a detector checking only one will miss half the violations. Both of this contract's confirmed live violations were measured 2026-08-19 and they fail on OPPOSITE axes — a rule covering only line-wrapping would clear sgs/icon-list as healthy, and a rule covering only text width would clear sgs/container as healthy.

vertical_wrapsTooManyLines.cause: a MULTI-WORD label breaks at its spaces and stacks into 3+ lines, exceeding the fixed 38px segment height
vertical_wrapsTooManyLines.example: sgs/container 'Full (no cap)' — 13 chars, 3 words, 3 rendered lines, 43px of text in a 38px box, crossing the top border by 3px and the bottom by 2px

horizontal_singleWordTooWide.cause: a SINGLE UNBREAKABLE word has no space to wrap at, so instead of stacking it spills sideways past its segment into its neighbours
horizontal_singleWordTooWide.example: sgs/icon-list 'Numbered' — 8 chars, 1 word, 1 rendered line, 62px of text in a 47px segment, overflowing by 15px. This is the visual collision originally reported as the labels 'running together'.
horizontal_singleWordTooWide.detect: max(rect.width for rect in Range.getClientRects()) > segment.getBoundingClientRect().width

twoDistinctFailureModes.counterIntuitiveConsequence: A LONGER label can be safe while a SHORTER one fails. 'Full (no cap)' (13 chars) and 'Numbered' (8 chars) both fail; 'Custom…' (7 chars) passes at a comparable segment width. What matters is the longest UNBREAKABLE run of characters and how many break-points exist, never the total length.

shapeRule.howADetectorShouldCheckThis: Measure, do not estimate, and check BOTH axes in one pass. Element height/width are USELESS here — every segment span reports the full segment box (38px tall) regardless of what it contains, because it stretches to fill its slot; that is exactly what made an earlier 'two lines' reading wrong. Use Range.selectNodeContents(textNode).getClientRects(), which returns one rect per RENDERED LINE: `rects.length >= 3` is the vertical violation, `max(r.width) > segment.width` is the horizontal one. A static source-only detector CANNOT do this — wrapping and text width depend on font metrics, segment width and option count together, so it needs a real browser against the real rendered control. Not built this session; both known violations were found by running this measurement by hand.
shapeRule.explicitlyNotAFormula: Two attempts at a precise px-per-character width-budget formula were tried and abandoned this session (see _corrected_2026_08_19_v2) — a per-character constant derived from one word does not transfer to another. The line-count ceiling in rule (b) replaces that entirely: it is directly measurable, needs no constant, and does not care how the characters are distributed.

knownLiveViolations.finding: Its own 5-option ToggleGroupControl (Icon/Emoji/Bullet/Numbered/None) breaches rule (c) — HORIZONTAL overflow. Measured live 2026-08-19: 'Numbered' renders 62px wide on a single line inside a 47px segment, spilling 15px into its neighbours. It stays on 1 line precisely BECAUSE it is one unbreakable word, so a line-count-only check would wrongly clear it. Siblings measured healthy with 14-22px of spare width ('Icon' 24px, 'Emoji' 32px, 'Bullet' 32px, 'None' 32px).
knownLiveViolations.fixDirection: NOT decided or applied this session — a shorter single word (e.g. 'Number') would satisfy rule (c) at this segment width without changing the control type. Copy decision for Bean, not a mechanical swap.

knownLiveViolations.finding: Its own 4-option ToggleGroupControl (Normal/Wide/'Full (no cap)'/'Custom…') breaches rule (b) — 'Full (no cap)' (13 chars, three words) renders on THREE lines in a 38px segment (43px of text), crossing the top border by 3px and the bottom border by 2px. Its siblings are all 1 line with ~10px clearance, so this is a single-outlier failure, not a control-wide sizing problem. Measured live on the deployed canary via Range.getClientRects(); source is WidthPanel.js:28. ⚠ An earlier version of this entry said 'wraps to two visual lines' — that was an eyeball estimate from a screenshot and it was wrong; the measurement says three.

predictVsMeasuredReconciliation_2026_08_.predicted: 71 (55 direct mounts + 16 credited to the 4 extension surfaces conditional-visibility.js/fx.js/hover-effects.js/parallax.js, per this row's own adoption figure)
predictVsMeasuredReconciliation_2026_08_.measured: 66 CONFORMANT via the live census run against a temporary local merge — 5 below prediction
predictVsMeasuredReconciliation_2026_08_.rule: Per this project's own standing discipline: a measured count BELOW an independent prediction is a detector bug until proven otherwise — not silently accepted as 'close enough'.
predictVsMeasuredReconciliation_2026_08_.rootCause: PROVEN, not assumed. `conditional-visibility.js` mounts its ToggleControls via a GLOBAL `addFilter('editor.BlockEdit', ...)` with NO per-block gate at all (confirmed by reading the file — no `enabledExtensions`/`hideExtensions` check anywhere in it, unlike `hover`/`background`/`width` etc., which DO gate through `supports.sgs.enabledExtensions`). It therefore reaches all 83 blocks, including every one of the 17 blocks the census marked VIOLATION (spot-checked: sgs/tabs and sgs/process-steps both declare NO `enabledExtensions` at all in block.json, so they cannot be reaching it through the gated mechanism the census's shared resolver understands — they reach it through this ungated global HOC instead). The census's `resolveComponentFiles` reach model can see a block's own edit.js plus components it imports plus the gated extension surfaces, but has no way to attribute a universally-applied `editor.BlockEdit` filter back to an individual consuming block.
predictVsMeasuredReconciliation_2026_08_.verdict: Confirmed detector limitation, not a golden-row defect. The 17 'VIOLATION' blocks genuinely do have a working ToggleControl (several, from conditional-visibility.js alone) — the census undercounts by construction for this one mechanism. Recorded here rather than silently accepted so a future engine improvement knows exactly what's missing: a way to attribute an ungated `editor.BlockEdit`-style extension surface to every block, distinct from the already-solved `enabledExtensions`-gated case.

icon.reasoning: No competitor exists — confirmed by a full-file read this session (477 lines) AND a live check for a core equivalent. WordPress core ships no generic arbitrary-icon-library picker: the nearest thing, core's Social Icons block, only offers a small fixed set of named social platforms, not a general browsable icon library. IconPicker is a genuinely bespoke modal (4 icon libraries — Lucide 1,917, Emoji 1,914, WordPress icons, Dashicons — search, categories, windowed rendering, full keyboard/screen-reader support) built because the gap is real. Live-verified 2026-08-19 in the sandybrown canary editor (sgs/icon block): a 'Choose an icon' modal with library tabs, category sidebar, search box and a live filterable grid.

shapeRule.rule1: label, value, onChange required; id REQUIRED and MISSING — re-verified fresh this session, not just copied forward. Signature at IconPicker.js:143-148 takes no id prop at all; the BaseControl mount at IconPicker.js:335 passes only label and __nextHasNoMarginBottom, no id/htmlFor.

multi-select.reasoning: FormTokenField itself is the right underlying primitive — confirmed correct for its designed case (name<->ID resolution for an open/searchable term set). The wrapper does not change that; it fixes a real interaction gap found live. Confirmed live 2026-08-19 (Bean asked to see it directly, since an EMPTY FormTokenField is visually indistinguishable from a plain TextControl — both are just a bordered box with a label and help text until a token exists): DOM class is genuinely `components-form-token-field`, and typing an exact/suggested term + Enter produces a real removable chip (screenshotted: 'Uncategorized ×').

fixedUxGap_2026_08_19.finding: Typing a value that does NOT exactly match an existing term (e.g. a partial string with no suggestion arrow-selected) and pressing Enter silently cleared the input — no chip, no error, no feedback. Confirmed by direct interaction before the fix: typing the full nonexistent string 'Test Category' + Enter did nothing; typing the partial 'Uncat' + Enter without arrowing down to the suggestion ALSO did nothing; only 'Uncat' + ArrowDown + Enter produced a chip.
fixedUxGap_2026_08_19.fix: SgsMultiSelectField sets two REAL FormTokenField props, verified against the component's own README before use (not guessed): `__experimentalAutoSelectFirstMatch` so Enter now commits the top matching suggestion even without an explicit arrow-down (matching how a client actually expects a type-ahead field to behave), and `messages.__experimentalInvalid` so assistive tech gets a real announcement for a genuinely non-matching entry instead of silence.
fixedUxGap_2026_08_19.notVerifiedLive: The behaviour change (auto-select-first-match actually firing on Enter) was NOT re-tested live this session after the retrofit — this session's own rule bans `npm run build`, and the editor runs compiled `build/`, not `src/`. Correct at the source level, confirmed against the real prop contract, not confirmed by re-running the exact interaction that found the bug.

reasoning.problem: Survey found 5 real date-holding attributes, ALL currently rendered via raw TextControl — a genuine gap, not the ideal shape. 3 are type-constrained (sgs/countdown-timer.targetDate, type="datetime-local", edit.js:181-188; sgs/form-field-date.minDate/.maxDate, type="date", edit.js:99-112). 2 are uncontrolled freeform strings with no type attribute at all (sgs/testimonial.reviewDate, edit.js:712-719; sgs/timeline's repeater-item date field, edit.js:158-165, whose own help text explicitly documents accepting non-ISO freeform text — 'YYYY-MM-DD or e.g. January 2024').
reasoning.coreCheck: @wordpress/components ships DateTimePicker — a real calendar+clock widget (currentDate/onChange/is12Hour props, all optional). Confirmed live 2026-08-19 via the public Gutenberg Storybook (https://wordpress.github.io/gutenberg/iframe.html?id=components-datetimepicker--default, screenshotted): a full month calendar grid plus a TIME/DATE field pair plus a UTC-offset label. Core's own Post Publish panel uses exactly this component behind a trigger-button + Popover, not inline — the identical shape LinkPopoverField already established as precedent in this codebase (confirmed live 2026-08-19 in the sandybrown canary: sgs/icon's Link control is a compact 'Add link' trigger row opening a Popover with core's LinkControl inside).
reasoning.whyNotCiteAnUnusedComponentBlindly: DateTimePicker had 0 mounts anywhere in src/ before this session (confirmed by grep). That is a DIFFERENT situation from StateToggleControl (0 mounts, dead/abandoned code, correctly excluded elsewhere in golden-controls.json from ever being cited as canonical) — DateTimePicker is a live, actively-maintained core component that was simply never reached for. A genuinely correct, real, native control that hasn't been adopted yet is a gap to close, not evidence it's the wrong choice.
reasoning.decision: Bean-approved live 2026-08-19: build DateTimePickerField now (see 'built' status above) rather than leave this as a documented-but-unbuilt target.
